rules.h1sub: Dice game rules & how to play
rules.setupLead: You don’t need much, and a round with friends takes about half an hour.
rules.setup1: 5 dice – ideally with a dice cup.
rules.setup2: One score sheet per player with the 13 boxes from this page (any piece of paper will do) and a pen.
rules.setup3: 1 to 6 players. Alone, you play for your high score.
rules.setupP: Everyone rolls once with all five dice: the highest total starts. Play goes clockwise, and the game lasts exactly 13 rounds – one for every box.
rules.setupCta: No score sheet at hand? Use the online score sheet – it adds everything up for you.
rules.turnLead: On your turn you roll up to three times. After that you must write a score in one box.
rules.s1p: Your first roll always uses all five dice.
rules.s2p: Put aside the dice you want to keep and roll the rest again. You may do this twice. Dice you kept may go back into the cup on the next roll.
rules.s3p: After the third roll at the latest, choose one free box and enter the points. You may also stop earlier.
rules.exAlt: Three rolls: first three fives are kept, then the 3 and 6 are rolled again, in the end there are four fives and a 2.
rules.exP: Mia keeps her three 5s and rolls the other two dice twice. In the end she has four 5s and a 2. Now she can choose: Fives for 20 points, or Four of a kind for 22. A box once filled can’t be used again.
rules.strikeP: You must write something down every turn. If no box fits your roll, enter 0 in a box of your choice – that box is “struck” for the rest of the game. Good boxes to sacrifice are Ones or Kniffel when time is running out.
rules.upLead: In the upper section you only count the dice with that number.
rules.upP: Example: you roll 4 4 4 2 6 and write it under Fours – that’s 12 points. The figure on the right shows the target: three of each number.
rules.bonusP: Bonus: If the upper section adds up to 63 or more, you get 35 extra points. That’s exactly three of every number – one more six can make up for a missing one.
rules.lowLead: In the lower section, the pattern of the dice counts. Gold dice are the ones that matter.
rules.lb_threeP: At least three dice show the same number. Score the total of all five dice.
rules.lb_fourP: At least four dice show the same number. Score the total of all five dice.
rules.lb_fullP: Three of one number and two of another. Always 25 points.
rules.lb_smallP: Four numbers in a row: 1‑2‑3‑4, 2‑3‑4‑5 or 3‑4‑5‑6. The fifth die doesn’t matter. 30 points.
rules.lb_largeP: Five numbers in a row: 1‑2‑3‑4‑5 or 2‑3‑4‑5‑6. 40 points.
rules.lb_kniffelP: All five dice show the same number. The best box: 50 points.
rules.lb_chanceP: Anything goes. Score the total of all five dice – your safety net for a bad roll.
rules.scoreLead: When all 13 boxes are filled, add up your score sheet:
rules.endP: After 13 rounds everyone has filled every box. The player with the highest grand total wins. A tie? Then share the win – or play a quick decider: one roll each, highest total wins.
rules.varLead: Kniffel is played slightly differently at every table. Agree before the first roll which of these rules you use:
rules.var1: Extra Kniffels: If you roll another Kniffel after the Kniffel box is already filled with 50, you get 50 bonus points each time.
rules.var2: Joker rule: An extra Kniffel can be used as a joker for Full house, Small or Large straight and scores the full points there – but only if the matching box of the upper section is already filled.
rules.var3: Top to bottom: Fill the boxes strictly in order from Ones to Chance. A lot more luck, a lot less planning.
rules.var4: Blind: Before your first roll, announce the box you’re playing for. Wrong? Then you score 0 there.
rules.var5: Triple Kniffel: Each player has three columns; the second counts double, the third triple. 39 rounds – for long evenings.
rules.var6: Saved rolls: Rolls you don’t use can be saved for a later turn (at most 3 in total).
rules.var7: Yatzy rules: The Scandinavian version also has One pair and Two pairs, a Small straight is only 1‑2‑3‑4‑5 (15 points), a Large one only 2‑3‑4‑5‑6 (20), and the upper bonus is 50.
rules.faq1q: Do I have to roll three times?
rules.faq1a: No. You may stop after the first or second roll and write down your score straight away.
rules.faq2q: Can I pick up dice I already put aside?
rules.faq2a: Yes. Before each roll you decide again which dice you keep and which go back into the cup.
rules.faq3q: Does a large straight also count as a small straight?
rules.faq3a: Yes. 1‑2‑3‑4‑5 contains four numbers in a row, so you may enter it as a Small straight for 30 – useful if the Large straight is already filled.
rules.faq4q: Is a Kniffel also a Full house?
rules.faq4a: By the basic rules, no: a Full house needs two different numbers. With the joker rule (see Variants) an extra Kniffel can count as a Full house.
rules.faq5q: Can I write a score in a box that doesn’t fit?
rules.faq5a: Only as a 0. That’s called striking the box, and you can’t use it again in this game.
rules.faq6q: What is the highest possible score?
rules.faq6a: Without extra Kniffels it’s 375 points: 105 in the upper section (five of each number), 35 bonus and 235 in the lower section.
rules.faq7q: Is Kniffel the same as Yahtzee?
rules.faq7a: Almost. Yahtzee is the American name, Yatzy the Scandinavian one; the boxes are basically the same, but bonuses and straights differ a little (see Variants). Kniffel and Yahtzee are also trademarks of commercial dice games; this page explains how to play with five ordinary dice.
rules.faq8q: How do I get better at Kniffel?
rules.faq8a: Aim for the 63 bonus early: three 5s or 6s in the upper section are worth a lot. Keep Chance as long as possible for an emergency, and strike Ones rather than an expensive box. More in the strategy guide.

goal: The goal: Fill all 13 boxes of your score sheet with the best possible rolls and end the game with the most points.

info.gearAlt: Five dice, a score sheet and a pen
info.intro: Kniffel takes five minutes to explain and is fun for everyone from kids to grandparents. Luck decides every roll, but if you keep the right dice and choose your boxes wisely, you’ll win more often. All you need is five dice and a piece of paper.

strategy.sub: Luck decides every roll – but not what you make of it. With these tips you’ll get the bonus more often, pick better boxes and waste fewer points.
strategy.principle: You have 13 turns for 13 boxes. Every roll asks one question: Where is this roll worth the most – now and for the rest of the game?
principleItems: The bonus decides most games. You get 35 points for a perfectly ordinary upper section – more than for a Full house.
Stay flexible. After the first roll, keep dice that work for several boxes: three 6s help with Sixes, Three and Four of a kind, and Kniffel.
Chance is your safety net. Use it up early and you’ll have to strike a good box later.
strategy.bonusLead: For 63 points in the upper section you need three dice of every number. Don’t track the total – just how far you are above or below par.
strategy.parP: Four 5s and four 6s more than make up for the weak Fours and Ones: +6 means the bonus is safe. Only two 6s (−6) and you have to win those points back elsewhere.
bonusItems: High numbers count the most. One 6 above par is worth as much as six 1s. So go for Fives and Sixes in the upper section early.
Three is enough, four is better. Entering three of a number in the upper section is never a mistake; two only for Ones or Twos.
Ones and Twos are your buffer. Falling short there costs at most 3 or 6 points against par.
strategy.keepLead: After the first roll you decide what you’re going for. Rules of thumb, from top to bottom:
keepItems: Three or four of a kind: keep them. They fit the upper section, Three or Four of a kind and Kniffel.
Four in a row (2-3-4-5 or 3-4-5-6): keep them and go for the Large straight – you already have the Small one.
Two pairs: keep both if Full house is still open. Otherwise keep the higher pair.
One pair: keep it if the matching upper box is still open. Rather give up a pair of 1s for a 5 or 6.
Nothing useful: keep 5s and 6s and roll again – that keeps Sixes, Three of a kind and Chance open.
strategy.oddsH: Your chances with two rolls left
strategy.oddsNote: Gold: keep, dashed: roll twice more. A Kniffel from scratch happens in barely 5 % of whole turns – don’t count on it, but take it when it comes.
strategy.boxesLead: At the end of a turn a roll often fits several boxes. Here’s how to decide:
boxes: Take fixed points when they come. Full house, straights and Kniffel always score the same – whatever the numbers.
High rolls into Three of a kind, low ones up top. Three 6s are worth a lot in Three of a kind; three 2s score hardly anything there, but under Twos they’re exactly par.
Four of a kind with low numbers? Four 2s belong under Twos (+2 on par), not in Four of a kind.
Chance only from about 22 points. Below that it’s too valuable – save it for a turn that fits nowhere else.
An early Kniffel of 1s? Enter it as Kniffel anyway: 50 points beat any upper box.
strategy.strikeLead: If you have to enter a 0, put it where it costs you least. Good sacrifices, roughly in this order:
strike: Ones – 5 points at most, and you only fall 3 short of par for the bonus.
Kniffel – when only a few rounds are left, the chance of rolling one is small.
Large straight – if the Small straight is already filled and the dice don’t fit.
Twos – as long as the bonus is still within reach.
strategy.strikeNever: Never strike early: Fives, Sixes and Chance. They score the most – and the bonus depends on the high numbers.
end: Count the open boxes. If you still need Full house and Large straight in the last rounds, go for the harder one first.
Work out the bonus. If you’re only a few points short of 63, aim for the last upper box on purpose.
Behind? Take risks. A Kniffel or a Large straight can turn the game around – small safe points can’t.
Ahead? Play it safe. Take fixed points and keep Chance open until the end.
mistakes: Using Chance on the first turn – then your safety net is gone.
Entering two 6s under Sixes – that’s already 6 points below par.
Taking Three of a kind with low numbers while the upper box is still open.
Chasing the Kniffel stubbornly when a Full house or straight is almost there.
Not doing the maths – whether the bonus is still possible decides what you strike.
